title: Firstperson Field Crew
one_liner: A managed crew that records diverse first-person household and trade task data for robotics labs, to spec.
speaker: Brett Adcock
context: Brett says data diversity, like someone hosing down a dog or painting a house, made the robot better at folding laundry. He adds that physical interaction data can't be scraped and has to be collected, audited, cleaned and annotated.
customer: Embodied-AI and robotics startups and university labs that need diverse egocentric task video in real homes and trades but have no field team
problem: Real-world human demonstration data in varied homes is a key input, but recruiting, briefing, consenting and quality-checking contributors is slow, messy work that small labs can't staff.
revenue_model: Per accepted hour of footage, about $60–$150 per hour delivered with metadata, or monthly retainers of $5,000–$20,000 per lab (estimate)
why_now: Brett says the models are now starved for data rather than architecture, that data scaling looks log-linear, and that Figure collects at large scale in-house. Smaller labs need the same input without building their own crew.
first_steps: Record 2 hours of sample footage yourself using a head-mounted camera and a written task protocol
Email 15 embodied-AI startups and lab leads offering a free 5-hour pilot dataset
Recruit 10 local contributors through a gig board using a clear consent form and fixed pay per task
cost_to_start: About 2–3 weeks and $500–$1,500 (estimate) for cameras, consent forms and a sample dataset
competition: Data-labeling firms and some crowdsourced egocentric video projects exist, and big robotics labs collect in-house.
risks: Privacy and consent problems inside homes. Labs may need force or glove sensor data that a camera can't capture. Big buyers keep collection in-house. Quality rejections can wipe out the margin.

tool.title: Capture Brief Builder
tool.one_liner: Turns a lab's data needs into a recording protocol, contributor checklist and price quote.
tool.demo: A lab enters the tasks it wants (for example 'load dishwasher'), the environment types, hours needed, camera setup and annotation level. The tool generates a numbered protocol per task, a contributor checklist and consent-form outline, a shot-diversity plan spread across home types, and an itemized quote using the operator's editable rates. If the visitor pastes an API key, AI drafts richer step lists; example mode works without one.
tool.data_plan: Requirements come from the customer and rates from the operator. Optional AI drafting uses a key the visitor pastes in; without one, the page runs on built-in templates.
acceptance: Entering 3 tasks and 40 hours, then clicking Generate, produces a protocol section for each task plus a diversity table that splits the hours across environment types
Changing the per-hour rate field updates the quote total immediately
With no API key, example mode fills every section and labels it as an example template
A consent checklist always appears and includes a line about faces and children in the home
The brief can be downloaded as Markdown, and the layout works at 375px width
